target_customer: Retail, restaurant and convenience chains and commercial real estate brokers choosing expansion sites in North America
problem: Chains pick new store locations with legacy, expensive consulting and scattered datasets. PiinPoint combines traffic, demographics and available commercial real estate in one SaaS tool.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription; 2014 plan was a three-month pilot then monthly fees starting at $3,000
product_category: Location analytics and site selection software

founders.name: Jim Robeson
prior_employers: Government relations role in Toronto (employer not named)
Economic development manager (per Entrepreneur, employer not named)

founders.name: Adam Saunders
founders.background_notes: Described as a developer of GIS mapping software in a July 2014 Entrepreneur article; education not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed ingestion and blending of traffic, demographic and real estate datasets plus forecasting, standard data engineering for a team of four.

defensibility.rationale: Data was licensed from third parties and the UI was copyable; value came from customer workflows and dataset partnerships.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch (2014-03) only refers to unnamed legacy solutions. The company is still operating in 2026 with large chain customers, so no incumbent absorbed it.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in March 2014 reported more than ten customers at launch, and Entrepreneur in July 2014 reported interest from US retailers with expansion plans willing to pay from $3,000 per month.

brand_strength.rationale: Double i spelling is distinctive but is easily confused with the generic word pinpoint and with other Pinpoint companies. No press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: PiinPoint stayed small and capital light, moving from a four person YC team in 2014 to about 20 people and a customer list of large restaurant, convenience and retail chains by 2026. It has not raised a verified large round or exited, so it reads as a durable niche SaaS business rather than a venture scale outcome. Founder domain experience in economic development helped early sales.
notes: Outcome search found no acquisition, layoffs or shutdown. Aggregators (Bounce Watch) list a $1.4M seed on 2014-09-25 with BDC, Real Ventures and YC, while CB Insights lists $40K; neither confirmed by press, so unverified and not recorded as rounds. No named competitor in any source dated near the 2014 batch, so the list is empty.
